channel.title: ESSD - recent papers
channel.description: Combined list of the recent articles of the journal Earth System Science Data and the recent discussion forum Earth System Science Data Discussions

item.title: Italian Fluvial Sediment Transport Database: a comprehensive hub for archiving and analyzing hydrological data
item.description:
Italian Fluvial Sediment Transport Database: a comprehensive hub for archiving and analyzing hydrological data
Marco Luppichini, Francesco Comiti, Andrea Andreoli, Barbara Aldighieri, Paolo Billi, Irene Maria Bollati, Andrea Brenna, Diletta Chirici, Paolo Ciavola, Silvia Cilli, Marco Donnini, Simona Francalanci, Lorenzo Innocenti, Laura Longoni, Luca Mao, Ivan Marchesini, Ilenia Murgia, Giacomo Pellegrini, Daniele Penna, Lorenzo Picco, Riccardo Rainato, Leonardo Schippa, Luca Solari, Gianluca Tronti, Bruno Testa, Matteo Verdone, and Monica Bini
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7021–7041, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7021-2026, 2026
Rivers carry sediment that shapes landscapes and coasts, but in Italy these data are scattered and often incomplete. We created a national database and online platform to gather and organize past and present sediment measurements in one place. By linking data with clear information about where, when, and how they were collected, we made them easier to explore and compare over time.

item.title: A global dataset of soil microplastics (2005–2026)
item.description:
A global dataset of soil microplastics (2005–2026)
Peiwen Wu, Yang Su, Mengru Wang, Xiaomei Yang, Matthias C. Rillig, Xiahui Wang, Ruiping Liu, Su Ye, Lianqing Zhou, Zhou Shi, and Songchao Chen
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-536,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Plastic pollution poses a major threat to soils worldwide, yet global tracking remains fragmented. To address this, we built a global database by compiling over 6,000 records across 49 countries. We found that reported plastic amounts are highly uneven globally and vary significantly based on the detection method used. This standardized database provides a vital foundation for scientists and policymakers to map, monitor, and manage the ecological risks of soil pollution globally.

item.title: A knowledge-guided daily multi-layer soil freeze-thaw dataset for the Northern Hemisphere during 1950-2025
item.description:
A knowledge-guided daily multi-layer soil freeze-thaw dataset for the Northern Hemisphere during 1950-2025
Han Yu, Mousong Wu, Dongjie Yin, Youhua Ran, and Yonghong Yi
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-683,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
To extend soil freeze-thaw records beyond the satellite era, we developed a daily 0.1° dataset for Northern Hemisphere frozen-ground regions from 1950 to 2025 at depths of 10, 30, and 50 cm. A knowledge-guided neural network combined process-based simulations with in situ observations and achieved 86-90% accuracy in independent evaluation. The dataset provides a consistent basis for analyses of multi-decadal freeze-thaw changes and their vertical propagation through the upper soil profile.

item.title: SCS-TCWave: an event-based hindcast dataset of typhoon waves and reconstructed wind fields for the South China Sea (1979–2025)
item.description:
SCS-TCWave: an event-based hindcast dataset of typhoon waves and reconstructed wind fields for the South China Sea (1979–2025)
Feifan Fang, Yifeng Yang, Peng Jin, and Binzhen Zhou
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-737,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Typhoons generate the largest ocean waves in the South China Sea, but existing open data cannot capture how big these waves get near a storm's centre. We rebuilt the winds of 480 typhoons (1979–2025), simulated the waves they generated, and checked the results against tens of thousands of satellite and buoy measurements. The result is a free, open dataset showing, storm by storm, where extreme waves occur and how high they reach, supporting safer coasts, shipping, and offshore wind energy.

item.title: A harmonized radiocarbon chronology framework for subarctic North Pacific marine sediment cores
item.description:
A harmonized radiocarbon chronology framework for subarctic North Pacific marine sediment cores
Rong Wang, Jian Ren, and Bernhard Diekmann
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-742,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Marine sediment records reveal past ocean changes, but differences in their age models make comparisons difficult. We compiled published dating evidence and developed a common chronology framework for 17 sediment cores in the subarctic North Pacific. The released age tables and uncertainty estimates make existing records easier to compare and reuse, while documenting the limits of their age estimates.

item.title: AGPC: an Annual 500 m Gridded Population (1990–2020) for China incorporating 3D building volume dynamics
item.description:
AGPC: an Annual 500 m Gridded Population (1990–2020) for China incorporating 3D building volume dynamics
Xiaocong Xu, Shiyu He, Jinpei Ou, Yan Zhou, and Xiaoping Liu
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6995–7019, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6995-2026, 2026
We developed annual population maps for mainland China from 1990 to 2020 at 500-metre detail. A key advance is the use of changing three-dimensional building volume, allowing the maps to distinguish densely populated areas with extensive high-rise development that conventional maps based mainly on two-dimensional built-up land may overlook. Combined with census and other data, the maps show high accuracy and can support studies of urban growth, environmental change, and disaster risk.

item.title: Extending daily river discharge records across China using satellite-derived river widths
item.description:
Extending daily river discharge records across China using satellite-derived river widths
Yong Wang, Yulin Gong, Yinghong Jing, Xiaojun She, and Yao Li
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6973–6993, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6973-2026, 2026
Rivers are vital sources of freshwater, but long-term records of how much water they carry are unavailable for many regions. This study combined satellite imagery with observations from more than 1000 river gauges to create the most comprehensive daily river discharge dataset for China (1990–2024). The dataset reveals widespread declines in river discharge across much of the country and provides an important resource for water management, environmental research, and future satellite missions.

item.title: A National Depth-Resolved Soil-Moisture-to-Electromagnetic Proxy Database for Hydrogeophysical Monitoring
item.description:
A National Depth-Resolved Soil-Moisture-to-Electromagnetic Proxy Database for Hydrogeophysical Monitoring
Diaa Sheishah, Enas Abdelsamei, Viktoria Blanka-Vegi, Károly Barta, Ahmed M. Ali, Khaldoun Abualhin, Djamil Al-Halbouni, Wouter Dorigo, and Gyorgy Sipos
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-563,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Soil moisture controls drought, crop water supply, and groundwater recharge, but it is difficult to monitor below the surface. We used national monitoring data from 117 stations and six soil depths to build an open database that links soil moisture, soil type, water retention, and expected electromagnetic responses. The results identify a key mid-depth buffering zone and provide a practical reference for future drought monitoring, irrigation planning, and non-invasive soil-water surveys.

item.title: A dataset of high–spatiotemporal–resolution dust and non–dust aerosol mass concentration profiles from ground–based remote sensing in central China (2018–2024)
item.description:
A dataset of high–spatiotemporal–resolution dust and non–dust aerosol mass concentration profiles from ground–based remote sensing in central China (2018–2024)
Zhuang Wang, Chengxiao Liu, Yanfeng Huo, Xinfeng Lin, Shaowei Yan, Xiaoyun Sun, Jiaqi Chen, Nan Ge, Guanyin Yang, Zhenzhen Hua, Hao Zhang, Chune Shi, Yong Zhu, Yizhi Zhu, Congzi Xia, Kaidi Zhang, Xintong Chen, Yujia Chen, Chengzhi Xing, and Cheng Liu
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-677,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Airborne particles affect air quality and climate, but their distribution with height is poorly documented over central China. We used seven years of continuous ground-based lidar observations to build a detailed record of dust and other particles profiles from 2018 to 2024. Most particles were found below about two kilometres, with dust more common in spring and other particles in winter. The dataset can help track air pollution and dust transport and improve satellite and model assessments.

item.title: A random forest isoscape model of bioavailable Sr for South America: a focus on southern Brazil
item.description:
A random forest isoscape model of bioavailable Sr for South America: a focus on southern Brazil
Cinzia Scaggion, Tommaso Giovanardi, László Palcsu, Daniel Loponte, Mirian Carbonera, Sara Bernardini, Stefano Benazzi, Giulia Marciani, Marcos Cesar Pereira Santos, Eugenio Bortolini, Anna Cipriani, and Federico Lugli
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6925–6943, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6925-2026, 2026
In this work, we present a new dataset of strontium isotopes from leaves collected in Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul (Brazil). We combine these data with published South American records to produce a machine learning–based map of strontium isotope distribution across the continent. The dataset and model support studies of ancient mobility, provenance, and environmental and ecological processes.

item.title: Improving global and regional ocean heat content by consistently combining GRACE gravity, satellite altimetry and Argo profile observations in a joint inversion framework
item.description:
Improving global and regional ocean heat content by consistently combining GRACE gravity, satellite altimetry and Argo profile observations in a joint inversion framework
Bernd Uebbing, Kristin Vielberg, Roelof Rietbroek, Bene Aschenneller, Armin Köhl, and Jürgen Kusche
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6945–6972, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6945-2026, 2026
About 90% of the excess heat in the Earth system is stored within the oceans leading to significant ocean warming and corresponding (volumetric) sea level change. We quantify global and regional ocean heat content change (OHC) by consistently combining space-geodetic altimetry, gravity and in situ temperature profile observations. Our results agree well with published estimates and highlight the benefit of consistently processing space-geodetic datasets for deriving high quality OHC estimates.

item.title: A global terrestrial water budget discrete grid dataset constrained by GRDC observations (2000–2020)
item.description:
A global terrestrial water budget discrete grid dataset constrained by GRDC observations (2000–2020)
Kai Li, Juanle Wang, Congrong Li, Xianglin Ji, and Lizhi Pan
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-497,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Measurements from different satellites, models, and field records often give inconsistent pictures of land water conditions. We combined multiple global data sources with river measurements from thousands of basins to create monthly maps of rain, evaporation, river flow, and stored water from 2000 to 2020. The new data set reduced water balance mismatches and agreed better with river and field observations. It can support studies of water resources, droughts, floods, and climate impacts.

item.title: TEMPL: a Multi-Platform LiDAR Dataset of a Temperate Forest in the Eastern United States
item.description:
TEMPL: a Multi-Platform LiDAR Dataset of a Temperate Forest in the Eastern United States
Sangyoon Park, Zachary Nelson Horve, Cameron Patrick Wingren, Michael R. Saunders, Chunxi Zhao, Sang-Yeop Shin, John Evan Flatt, Ayman Habib, and Songlin Fei
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-632,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Forests are measured with different laser scanning systems, but comparable data from the same trees are rare. We created a public dataset from nine plots in the Central Hardwood Forest of the eastern United States using aircraft, drones, backpacks, and field surveys. It includes 838 individual-tree point clouds representing 231 trees. The point clouds were spatially aligned, allowing the same trees to be compared across views. The dataset can support forest measurement and ecological research.

item.title: A decade-scale catalog of coherent atmospheric infrasound transients from a three-element array at Jang Bogo Station, Terra Nova Bay, East Antarctica (2017–2026)
item.description:
A decade-scale catalog of coherent atmospheric infrasound transients from a three-element array at Jang Bogo Station, Terra Nova Bay, East Antarctica (2017–2026)
Yongcheol Park, Jinhoon Jung, and Won Sang Lee
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-647,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Antarctica is difficult to monitor continuously, especially through winter and bad weather. We assembled a decade-long record of 23,768 low-frequency atmospheric sound events recorded at Jang Bogo Station from 2017 to 2026. The open dataset includes timing, direction, signal strength, and waveform information, providing a new resource for studying changes in the Antarctic coastal environment and for testing infrasound monitoring methods.

item.title: Daily Precipitation-Frequency Estimates under Climate Oscillations across the Conterminous United States
item.description:
Daily Precipitation-Frequency Estimates under Climate Oscillations across the Conterminous United States
Ali Takallou, Nibedita Samal, and Hamid Moradkhani
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-726,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Extreme precipitation can threaten communities and infrastructure, and its frequency varies across regions and with large-scale climate patterns. We created a new high-resolution dataset for the conterminous United States by combining long-term precipitation records with spatial and climate information. Large-scale climate patterns can alter the frequency of extreme precipitation by up to 40 % in some regions, with important implications for flood-risk assessment and infrastructure planning.

item.title: SPAMS10: an InSAR-derived soil motion parameter dataset to model relative peat surface elevation changes
item.description:
SPAMS10: an InSAR-derived soil motion parameter dataset to model relative peat surface elevation changes
Yustisi Lumban-Gaol and Ramon Hanssen
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6913–6923, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6913-2026, 2026
Peat soils are sinking as groundwater levels drop, risking damage to farms, homes, and the environment. We combined ground measurements and satellite images to track how peat surfaces move over time. Using these data, we developed an open dataset that describes peat movement with a few key parameters and weather information. This dataset helps researchers and decision-makers better understand peat behaviour and assess actions to limit subsidence and protect the environment.

item.title: Methane Inversion inter-Comparison (MICA): A Multi-model Estimation of Regional and National Emissions in Asia
item.description:
Methane Inversion inter-Comparison (MICA): A Multi-model Estimation of Regional and National Emissions in Asia
Fenjuan Wang, Shamil Maksyutov, Rajesh Janardanan, Dmitry A. Belikov, Prabir K. Patra, Ruosi Liang, Yuzhong Zhang, Ge Ren, Hong Lin, Nicole Montenegro, Antoine Berchet, Marielle Saunois, Adrien Martinez, Sara Hyvärinen, Aki Tsuruta, Samuel Takele Kenea, Miao Liang, Xin Lan, Yukio Terao, M. Kawser Ahmed, Manish Naja, Akihiko Ito, Isamu Morino, Yukio Yoshida, Yu Someya, Tazu Saeki, and Tsuneo Matsunaga
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-420,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Methane is a potent greenhouse gas driving climate change, yet Asian emissions remain highly uncertain. We conducted the first Methane Inversion inter-Comparison for Asia (MICA) combining seven models to estimate methane across Asia from 2010 to 2021 using satellite and ground data. We found that emissions are generally lower than prior inventories, though some countries underreport. This study provides a comprehensive, transparent dataset to quantify regional methane budgets across Asia.

item.title: The Global Database of Deep-time Sedimentary Mercury Concentrations and Isotope Compositions (DeepSedHg)
item.description:
The Global Database of Deep-time Sedimentary Mercury Concentrations and Isotope Compositions (DeepSedHg)
Yuchen Yang, Songjing Li, Wang Zheng, Yi Liu, Jiubin Chen, and Ruoyu Sun
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-511,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Mercury preserved in sedimentary rocks records important changes in Earth's environment over billions of years. We created the first global database of these records by compiling and standardizing data from nearly 200 published studies. The database covers about 2.7 billion years of Earth's history and provides an open resource for studying environmental change, volcanic activity, and the evolution of the Earth system. It will support future research across many areas of Earth science.

item.title: PRECISi: A High-Resolution Daily Gridded Precipitation Dataset for Sicily (1951–2022) Derived from a Doubly Conditional Geostatistical Framework
item.description:
PRECISi: A High-Resolution Daily Gridded Precipitation Dataset for Sicily (1951–2022) Derived from a Doubly Conditional Geostatistical Framework
Niloufar Beikahmadi, Antonio Francipane, Dario Treppiedi, and Leonardo Valerio Noto
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-679,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Researchers created the first long-term, high-resolution daily rainfall dataset for Sicily, covering 1951 to 2022. It was built by combining historical rain-gauge records with a statistical method that is stratified based on local hydroclimatological regimes. Tests showed the dataset reliably detects rainy days and matches long-term climate averages. This resource can support water management and studies of climate change and extreme weather in the Mediterranean.

item.title: Gaussian-process fusion of ICESat-2 and SMOS/SMAP data for daily estimates of Arctic sea ice thickness and volume
item.description:
Gaussian-process fusion of ICESat-2 and SMOS/SMAP data for daily estimates of Arctic sea ice thickness and volume
Alek Petty, Christopher Cardinale, Michel Tsamados, William Gregory, and Alex Cabaj
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-700,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We combine laser-altimeter measurements with daily passive-microwave estimates of thin ice using Gaussian-process regression. The resulting dataset provides complete daily Arctic sea ice thickness maps across seven winter growth seasons, substantially improving spatial and temporal coverage, particularly during autumn freeze-up. It also better represents thin ice and enables consistent estimates of Arctic sea ice volume.
